avertissement: Traductions automatiques des textes français ; chaque nombre a été vérifié contre le français. Les documents de la Ville sont en français et font foi.

canopee.description: Tree planting, greening, fighting the emerald ash borer and heat islands.
canopee.enBref: The City buys trees and has them planted on public land, and pays an organization to green private and institutional land. Boroughs are adding their own resources: park fund money, equipment rental, blue-collar crews. Variances also govern tree planting in two building projects.

etapes.texte: City council awards contracts to 7574479 Canada inc. and Terrassement Technique Sylvain Labrecque inc. to supply and plant 1,374 trees, then water, maintain and partly replace them. The maximum expense is $2,456,590.55, taxes included, for trees spread across seven boroughs.

Pierrefonds-Roxboro transfers up to $162,233.12 from its reserved fund for park purposes to buying trees and plants. City council pays $3,071,550 to the Société de verdissement du Montréal métropolitain to plant and maintain trees on private and institutional sites from March 24 to December 31, 2026.

Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve authorizes an extension at 1620, rue Préfontaine with 25 trees and 5% greening instead of the required 40 trees and 25%. Montréal-Nord allows trees to be planted less than 1.5 metres from the street line at 5745, boulevard Léger, for a two-storey building.

Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve rents a mini backhoe loader with operator for $152,916.75, taxes included, and sets aside $200,000 for additional blue-collar crews assigned to planting, from May to November 2026. Outremont entrusts URBEX Construction inc. with renovating the parc Pratt chalet and redeveloping its surroundings, including plant installation, partly funded by the Programme de réfection et de verdissement des parcs locaux.

City council leases land in the Namur-Hippodrome neighbourhood, in Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce, to the Société de verdissement du Montréal métropolitain, for a total rent of $100 before taxes. The organization stores materials, equipment and trees intended for planting there.

aSurveiller.texte: The Société de verdissement du Montréal métropolitain must submit its accountability report by December 31, 2026 at the latest, then its report and financial statements by March 31, 2027.
The Namur-Hippodrome neighbourhood nursery lease runs until April 30, 2028.

deneigement.description: Snow removal and snow loading contracts, spreading of abrasives, parking by-laws.

etapes.titre: Spring cleaning of streets and sidewalks
etapes.texte: Several boroughs are renting sweeper trucks, tanker trucks, sidewalk washers and a mini sweeper with operators to remove abrasives after winter. Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve is authorizing spending of $574,920.99, taxes included, for four sweeper trucks and three tanker trucks in 2026 and 2027.

etapes.titre: Snow removal from downtown public squares
etapes.texte: Ville-Marie is hiring companies to maintain, clean and remove snow from Square Viger, Place des Montréalaises, square Dorchester, place du Canada, îlot Bonaventure, square Victoria, place du Sable-Gris and square Chaboillez. The borough is also extending snow removal for the Quartier des Spectacles by one year, from April 2, 2026 to April 1, 2027.

Montréal-Nord is paying for an additional rented grader during the 2025-2026 winter, and Saint-Léonard is allocating $200,000 in surplus to its 2026 snow removal operations, after 39 abrasive spreading operations since November 15, 2025, while the budget had planned for 20. The City and some boroughs are extending 12-month turnkey snow removal, towing and equipment rental with operators contracts.

etapes.titre: Snow removal from parks and buildings
etapes.texte: The City is extending snow removal for the parking lot of the édifice Jacinthe-Fyfe and for parc Frédéric-Back, the TAZ and the stade de soccer de Montréal. It is also awarding a contract to remove snow from service roads and parking lots in the Grand parc de l'Ouest, in the Anse-à-l'Orme, Bois-de-la-Roche and Cap-Saint-Jacques sectors.

aSurveiller.texte: Snow removal services for the Grand parc de l'Ouest cover two seasons, from November 1, 2026 to April 30, 2028.
The extended towing contracts begin on November 15, 2026.
The turnkey snow removal contract for Le Plateau-Mont-Royal ends on April 15, 2031, with each season running from November 1 to April 15.
The turnkey snow removal contracts for Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce, Lachine, Outremont and Le Sud-Ouest end on April 15, 2030.

eau-egouts.description: Pipes, drinking water production plants, Jean-R.-Marcotte wastewater treatment plant, retention basins.
eau-egouts.enBref: This year, the City is financing and carrying out work on its water networks: waterworks and sewer pipes, replacement of lead service lines, drinking water production plants and the Jean-R.-Marcotte wastewater treatment plant. It is awarding contracts for the reconstruction and rehabilitation of pipes on streets in many boroughs. It is also moving forward with the ozone disinfection project for wastewater discharged into the Saint-Laurent river.

etapes.texte: The City is raising to $381,000,000 the loan financing the disinfection unit at the Jean-R.-Marcotte wastewater treatment plant. The money is to be used to finish the ozonation unit, install liquid oxygen tanks and build the oxygen plant.

The City is awarding contracts to rehabilitate secondary water pipes without trenching, redo roadways and sidewalks, and replace lead water service connections. The targeted streets are notably in Pierrefonds-Roxboro, Saint-Laurent, Ahuntsic-Cartierville, Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension, Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce, Le Plateau-Mont-Royal and Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve.

The City is retaining Pure Technologies ltd. to install fibre optics and continuously monitor 38 kilometres of prestressed concrete trunk pipes for ten years. City council takes a step toward a $951,000,000 loan by-law for the renewal of secondary waterworks and sewer networks from 2027 to 2031.

aSurveiller.texte: Announced adoption of the $951,000,000 loan by-law for secondary waterworks and sewer networks, on October 19, 2026.
Shutdown of sludge incinerator 4 at the Jean-R.-Marcotte plant in January 2027, for about six weeks of work.
Completion of water pipe work on rue de la Cathédrale pushed back to March 2027.
Rue Guy construction site planned until December 2027.
Commissioning of the ozone plant at the Jean-R.-Marcotte plant expected in 2029; contracts for lots 4, 5 and 6 must end in the last quarter of 2028.

frederic-back.titre: Frédéric-Back Park and Saint-Michel Environmental Complex
frederic-back.description: The former quarry turned dump, being transformed into a park in phases: urban greenhouses, biogas capture, electrical system upgrades.

etapes.titre: Funding request for an east-west link
etapes.texte: The City is asking the Quebec Ministère des Transports et de la Mobilité durable for funding of up to $2,000,000 for a 900-metre multi-use trail crossing the park, with a footbridge about 150 metres long. The project also includes rainwater management structures and a 12.7-hectare meadow.

The urban agglomeration council approves construction of a greenhouse complex, valued at $2,185,000, then assigns the work to the city council, which awards it to the Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension borough. In July, the borough awards Les industries Harnois inc. a contract worth $499,865.92 to supply and install two greenhouses.

The City awards Systèmes Urbains inc. a contract worth $1,091,693.37 for the second phase of electrical work at the Complexe environnemental de Saint-Michel. The work includes a new 25 kV power supply, a transformer, a backup generator, and an automated system to manage biogas capture.

The borough awards Groupe MPotvin the redevelopment of rue De Louvain between the park and boulevard Saint-Michel, for a maximum of $8,199,514.82. The work covers sewers, water mains, lighting, sidewalks, cycling facilities, and plantings.

Two companies are awarded 30-month contracts for general maintenance and ecological and horticultural management of the park. The City is also extending, by five months, the rental of a compost screener and a loader tractor, for an additional $296,349.21; the compost is used in particular for park landscaping.
The City is extending by six months the snow removal contract for Frédéric-Back Park, the TAZ, and the soccer stadium, awarded to 178001 Canada inc. (Groupe Nicky), for an additional $193,215.49.

aSurveiller.texte: The call for projects under the Ministère des Transports' funding program, for the footbridge and the east-west link, closes on November 26, 2026.
Greenhouse installation work must be completed by December 2026; commissioning is announced for winter 2027.
The Boisé Ouest sector, covering 26 hectares, is to be added in 2027 to the 65 hectares already open to the public.
The snow removal extension covers the period from November 1, 2026, to April 30, 2027.
Work on rue De Louvain continues from May to October 2027 (sidewalks, curbs, bump-outs), then from May to August 2028 (final roadway, bike path, plantings).

grand-parc-ouest.description: The largest municipal park in Canada, in the process of being assembled: land acquisitions, Anse-à-l'Orme, Cap-Saint-Jacques, Bois-de-la-Roche, parc-nature des Sources.

etapes.texte: The City is adding $162,897.98, taxes included, to the contract for repairing the heritage walls on chemin de Senneville, bringing the contract to $1,174,331.77, taxes included. The file explains the costs through unforeseen site conditions: buried stones that had to be cleaned by hand, extra mortar, sod, and a deteriorated culvert that needs replacing.

The City is submitting an application for the Cap-Saint-Jacques sector (330 hectares) for the international Urban Night Sky Place designation from DarkSky International. The application involves no spending; if the designation is granted, the City commits to producing a lighting plan, bringing its light fixtures up to standard, and keeping the site accessible at night.

etapes.titre: Two sectors listed as natural environments
etapes.texte: The parc-nature des Sources (38.32 ha) and the Anse-à-l'Orme sector of the Grand parc de l'Ouest (429 ha) are listed in the Répertoire des milieux naturels protégés et contributifs à la biodiversité for the urban agglomeration, with conservation plans. The 2025 report submitted shows 4,051 ha listed or provisionally listed, or 8.1% of the agglomeration's territory.

etapes.titre: Rebuilding the culvert on chemin Senneville
etapes.texte: A contract worth $366,117.31, taxes included, is awarded to Gendron Gestion Civil inc. to rebuild the culvert under chemin Senneville, as part of the modernization of the Bois-de-la-Roche agricultural hub; the total expenditure reaches $481,850.45, taxes included. The undersized culvert had been damaged by the heavy rains of August 2024.

etapes.titre: Snow removal, cleaning and tree felling
etapes.texte: The City is awarding Paysagiste Solarco inc. the snow removal contract for service roads and parking lots in the Anse-à-l'Orme, Bois-de-la-Roche and Cap-Saint-Jacques sectors ($178,330.82, taxes included), and 9232-3914 Québec inc. the cleaning of nine buildings at Cap-Saint-Jacques ($704,619.24, taxes included). Entrepreneur Paysagiste Strathmore (1997) ltée will fell ash trees and other dying trees in the park, for a total expenditure of $1,713,041.27, taxes included.

aSurveiller.texte: Snow removal of service roads and parking lots from November 1, 2026 to April 30, 2028.
Cleaning of nine buildings at Cap-Saint-Jacques from November 1, 2026 to October 31, 2030, with a possible extension to October 31, 2031.
Felling of ash trees and dying trees from fall 2026 to early summer 2028.
Cap-Saint-Jacques lighting management plan submitted in February 2027, response from DarkSky International expected in April 2027, full site compliance by April 2032.

itinerance.description: Support for organizations, warming centres and shelters for people experiencing homelessness.
itinerance.enBref: The City lends municipal buildings to organizations to open warming centres, and it funds organizations that work with people experiencing homelessness. It also deploys a Ville-Marie public works team to other boroughs for cleanliness interventions related to homelessness. It is setting up a framework to receive private donations and is appealing a ruling on the encampments under the Van Horne viaduct.

etapes.texte: The City lends three buildings free of charge to organizations for the winter: the church at 5600, 12e Avenue to the Centre des Femmes de convictions de Montréal, the former monastery of the Recluses Missionnaires at 12050, boulevard Gouin Est to Projets Autochtones du Québec, and the Bain St-Denis at 7075, rue Saint-Hubert to L'Amour en Action SYL DAN. The loans end on April 30, 2026, and the value of the unbilled rent is estimated at $57,076 for the church.

Verdun pays $12,950 to the Société de développement social to keep outreach workers in its municipal facilities from January 5 to February 6, 2026. Ahuntsic-Cartierville ratifies the continuation of the contract with Les services de cohabitation sociale COHAB inc. for a warming centre for winter 2025-2026.

The City grants financial support to community organizations under the Programme itinérance et milieux inclusifs 2026-2028, for inclusion, public space cohabitation and awareness projects. The amounts cover a three-year period ending December 31, 2028.

etapes.titre: Private donations and fit-up of the Bain St-Denis
etapes.texte: City council adopts a framework to receive private donations for housing, shelter and social cohabitation projects; donors do not choose which project is funded. Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie transfers $250,000 for the activities and fit-up work of the temporary warming centre at the Bain Saint-Denis. City council also adopts a declaration of support for people experiencing homelessness and a motion on a rent support fund.

etapes.titre: Encampments on rue Notre-Dame and appeal of the ruling
etapes.texte: The City awards a contract of $149,520, taxes included, to Mission Old Brewery to support people from the rue Notre-Dame encampment area toward shelter and housing, and pays $90,000 to the Réseau d'aide aux personnes seules et itinérantes de Montréal for the 2026, 2027 and 2028 editions of the Nuit des sans-abri. The executive committee takes charge of the dispute over the encampments under the Van Horne viaduct and authorizes an appeal of the June 8, 2026 ruling.

aSurveiller.texte: Mission Old Brewery's mandate in the rue Notre-Dame encampment area ends on October 18, 2026.
The agreement between Ville-Marie and Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles for the public works team runs until May 15, 2027.
Support under the Programme itinérance et milieux inclusifs ends on December 31, 2028.

louvain-est.description: The neighbourhood being built on municipal land in Ahuntsic-Cartierville: acquisitions, soil decontamination, street names, temporary layouts.

etapes.texte: The City is extending the lease of a piece of land to the Société de transport de Montréal for parking vehicles used by its agents, south of rue de Louvain and west of boulevard Saint-Laurent. It is also extending the lease of a neighbouring piece of land to a company for paid parking reserved for members of an app.

The Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension borough is awarding a company the redevelopment of rue de Louvain, between parc Frédéric-Back and boulevard Saint-Michel. The work affects sewers, water mains, lighting, traffic lights, sidewalks, the bike path and plantings.

etapes.titre: The main street becomes avenue des Solidarités
etapes.texte: City council is naming the new street at the heart of the eco-district "avenue des Solidarités." The name comes from a public call for proposals held in fall 2024.

The City is awarding a contract to build a road with sewer, water main, roadway, electrical network and lighting in the eco-district, as well as for the environmental management of the soil. It is adding $2,007,312.15 net, through the environmental liability reserve, to remediate the soil of the former gas station sector on the Louvain Est site.

The borough is adopting a draft resolution authorizing the demolition of a building on avenue de l'Esplanade and rue de Louvain Ouest, followed by the construction of a group of buildings with a minimum density of 200 housing units per hectare. It is also launching a draft by-law to increase the height and density allowed on part of the municipal land at 50 and 150, rue de Louvain Ouest.

aSurveiller.texte: The lease of the land rented to the Société de transport de Montréal for parking begins on October 1, 2026, for three years, at a rate of 92 days per year.
The free loan of the land for growing sunflowers and the greenhouse runs from November 1, 2026 to October 31, 2027.
The free loan of the community garden land continues until December 31, 2027.
The land at the corner of rue de Louvain Ouest and avenue de l'Esplanade would be loaned for programming activities from April 1 to October 31, 2027.

The rue de Louvain worksite between parc Frédéric-Back and boulevard Saint-Michel continues from May to October 2027 (sidewalks, curbs, bump-outs), then from May to August 2028 (final roadway, bike path, plantings).
The street-naming file indicates that the site's layout work is planned for around 2032 and that four other public places remain to be named.

matieres-residuelles.description: Collections, sorting centres, biomethanization and ecocentres.
matieres-residuelles.enBref: This year, the City is changing the days, sectors and frequency of collections in several boroughs, and buying bins for residents. It is extending its food waste treatment contracts and its ecocentre-related contracts, and awarding a contract to recover mattresses. It is also tabling the agglomeration's 2025 residual materials management report.

etapes.texte: The City extends twice, by six months each time, its contracts with Recyclage Notre-Dame inc. to compost or biomethanize food waste from the eastern part of the agglomeration. The materials are transferred in Montréal-Est and then treated in Saint-Thomas-de-Joliette and in Moose Creek, Ontario, while awaiting the commissioning of the Montréal-Est organic materials treatment centre.

etapes.titre: Bin purchases and loan of sorting equipment
etapes.texte: City council concludes agreements with Orbis Canada and USD Global to supply collection bins to residents of the boroughs, then with Plasti-Bac inc. for garbage bins intended for Ahuntsic-Cartierville and Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension. The executive committee approves an agreement with Tricentris, which pays $43,773.61, taxes included, for a program to loan reusable dishware, water fountains and sorting stations for neighbourhood events.

The agglomeration extends the contracts for garbage collection from front-loading and semi-underground containers, as well as the container contract for the écocentre Saint-Laurent. It awards Recyc-Matelas inc. a contract worth $734,690.25, taxes included, to collect and recover mattresses and box springs from ecocentres, assigns two firms studies on buildings located on former disposal sites, and extends the contract for the software that manages dumping authorizations.

aSurveiller.texte: The program to loan dishware, water fountains and sorting stations is offered until December 31, 2026 at the latest.
The extension of the food waste treatment contracts runs until February 28, 2027.
The container contract for the écocentre Saint-Laurent and the container collection contracts are extended until October 31, 2027.
The contract for the dumping authorization management software covers the period from October 12, 2026 to October 11, 2029.

namur-hippodrome.description: The new neighbourhood on the site of the former Blue Bonnets racetrack: sale of land, loan by-laws, waterworks in the Namur–De la Savane sector.
namur-hippodrome.enBref: The City is preparing the future neighbourhood on the site of the former Blue Bonnets racetrack, in Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce. It got an extra delay from Québec to sell a first piece of land, adopted two loan by-laws for waterworks and public domain works, and transferred a piece of land to an organization for non-market housing. At the same time, it is leasing parcels of the site to organizations for temporary uses.

etapes.titre: Deadline pushed back to sell a first piece of land
etapes.texte: The Québec government grants the City a delay until October 31, 2027 to sell a first piece of land on the site of the former racetrack, west of boulevard Décarie and south of rue Paré. The postponement does not bring any financial compensation, and the other conditions of the 2017 transfer deed stay the same.

City council approves a City guarantee of $2,000,000 to the Canada Infrastructure Bank, for a loan to Société GALOPH used to pay for feasibility studies of the residential project. The same day, council rejects a motion from the Official Opposition on governance and the management of assets and public funds in the neighbourhood's development.

The City borrows $29,000,000 to develop the neighbourhood's public domain: soil remediation, sewers and waterworks, street redevelopment, fees and land purchases. It also borrows $12,000,000 to build main waterworks pipes between boulevard Cavendish, in Saint-Laurent, and rue Isabella, in Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce.

etapes.titre: Four buildings authorized on rue Namur
etapes.texte: The borough of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce adopts a draft resolution authorizing the construction of four residential buildings in four phases, at 7301 boulevard Décarie and 5150-5160 rue Namur. One of the buildings must house a municipal sports and leisure centre, and the developer must pay $3,200,000 for public amenities and equipment in the sector.

The City leases parcels of the site to the community cafeteria MultiCaf and to the Coopérative de solidarité Polliflora for temporary urban agriculture, as well as to the Société de verdissement du Montréal métropolitain for a transition nursery. Each lease provides for a symbolic rent, and the organizations pay for development, upkeep and property taxes.

aSurveiller.texte: Deadline given by the Québec government to sell a first piece of land on the site: October 31, 2027.
The $128.3M federal grant is conditional on the infrastructure being completed by 2031; the funds from the $29,000,000 loan cover works from 2026 to 2028.
Communia has five years after the signing of the transfer deed to complete at least one building, and housing affordability must last at least 25 years.
End of temporary leases: April 30, 2027 for MultiCaf, March 31, 2028 for Polliflora, and April 30, 2028 for the transition nursery.

parcs.description: Development and renovation of parks, including the Grand parc de l'Ouest.
parcs.enBref: The City is designing and renovating parks in several boroughs: soil studies, work contracts, public art and adjustments to projects already underway. In the Grand parc de l'Ouest, it is having walls and a culvert repaired, submitting an application for a designation related to the night sky, and awarding contracts to companies for snow removal, cleaning, and tree felling. Several projects are funded by the participatory budget, the environmental liability reserve, or park funds.

etapes.titre: Design, soil studies and funding agreement
etapes.texte: The City awards a competition-winning team the design of the bibliothèque Caroline-Dawson and the redevelopment of the parc Le Prévost, for a total expense of $10,559,257.81 taxes included. It also pays $174,471.56 to Verdun for studies before redoing the parc Monseigneur-J.-A.-Richard, and the Sud-Ouest signs an agreement with Hydro-Québec to obtain $154,000 for the parc d'Argenson.

etapes.titre: Grand parc de l'Ouest: work and protection
etapes.texte: The City adds $162,897.98 to the contract to repair the heritage walls on chemin de Senneville and awards a contract to rebuild the culvert under that same road, in the pôle agricole du Bois-de-la-Roche. It submits the application for the Cap-Saint-Jacques sector for the Urban Night Sky Place designation and lists the Anse-à-l'Orme sector, along with the parc-nature des Sources, in the registry of protected natural environments.

The City adds $153,434.14 for construction supervision of the parc du Bassin-à-Bois and $168,472.14 to decontaminate the parc George-Vernot. The boroughs move or increase budgets for the parcs des Hirondelles, du Sault-au-Récollet, Villeray and Percy-Walters.

etapes.titre: Maintenance of the Grand parc de l'Ouest
etapes.texte: The agglomeration awards contracts for snow removal on service roads and parking lots in the Anse-à-l'Orme, Bois-de-la-Roche and Cap-Saint-Jacques sectors, cleaning of nine buildings at Cap-Saint-Jacques, and felling of ash trees and declining trees.

aSurveiller.texte: Selection of the winning public art project for the parc des Eaux-Cachées in October 2026, contract with the artist in December 2026, and installation of the work in 2028.
Adoption expected at city council on October 19, 2026 to transfer a 75.2 m² laneway strip to the parc Le Prévost.
Start of the Grand parc de l'Ouest snow removal and cleaning contracts on November 1, 2026.
Response from DarkSky International expected in April 2027 for Cap-Saint-Jacques, with the lighting plan to be submitted in February 2027.
Final acceptance of the parc du Bassin-à-Bois work expected in June 2027.
Completion of work on the parc J.O.R.-Leduc expected in June 2028.

pietonnisation.description: Pedestrian streets, public squares and business animation ordinances.
pietonnisation.enBref: This year, the City is funding and regulating temporary pedestrian streets on commercial arteries, mainly for the 2026 summer season. The executive committee paid $2,694,500 to the boroughs under the call for projects for pedestrianization on commercial arteries [CE26 0465], and the boroughs adopted the ordinances that close the streets, authorize terraces, sales and music. Other decisions concern public squares: development, change of status of a lot and an official name.

etapes.titre: Subsidy rules and settlement of a dispute
etapes.texte: Ville-Marie adopts a by-law allowing it to subsidize its business development corporations to pedestrianize streets, up to $425 per linear metre, provided council closes the street by ordinance [CA26 240037]. Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie settles out of court for $41,686.46 a lawsuit related to work on the public square at the corner of rue Beaubien Est and rue Boyer [CA26 26 0010].

The executive committee allocates $2,694,500 among boroughs for pedestrian streets closed for at least eight consecutive weeks, including rue Villeray as a new project [CE26 0465]. Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce creates the Placette CDN from April 1 to October 31, 2026 [CA26 170058] and Ville-Marie bans traffic on the sections of its summer pedestrianizations [CA26 240090].

The boroughs pay contributions to the business development corporations organizing the pedestrian streets: $102,045 for rue Villeray [CA26 14 0078], $375,500 for rue Sainte-Catherine Est [CA26 240134] and $67,500 for avenue Lacombe until 2028 [CA26 170108]. Outremont allocates $105,000 to the pedestrianization of avenue Bernard, in addition to a $106,000 grant from the Service du développement économique [CA26 16 0061].

Borough councils close their arteries to cars and regulate terraces, sales and noise: avenue Bernard from May 19 to September 24 [CA26 16 0082], avenues Royal and Madison from June 1 to October 31 [CA26 170088], rue Ontario Est from June 15 to September 18 [CA26 27 0115], avenues du Mont-Royal and Duluth [CA26 25 0134]. Ville-Marie adjusts the dates of three pedestrianizations [CA26 240155] and Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve removes 113 paid parking spaces [CA26 27 0119].

etapes.titre: Public squares and end of season
etapes.texte: City council changes the status of a 899 square metre lot at the corner of rue Sherbrooke Est and boulevard Langelier from street (public square) to local park [CM26 0888] and names the public square at the corner of rue Charleroi and avenue L'Archevêque « place Chez-Marguerite » [CM26 0913]. Ville-Marie authorizes the sound ambiance on the pedestrian streets of the Quartier des spectacles [CA26 240372] and Le Plateau-Mont-Royal revises the reopening schedule of avenue du Mont-Royal [CA26 25 227].

aSurveiller.texte: Avenue du Mont-Royal reopens to traffic between rue Saint-Denis and rue Resther on September 30, 2026, and between boulevard Saint-Laurent and rue Saint-Denis on October 15, 2026.
The boroughs must report on the amounts received for pedestrianizations in November 2026 and return unspent money in December 2026.
The ordinance on the sound ambiance of the pedestrian streets of the Quartier des spectacles runs until September 2, 2027.
The on-demand transit contract on avenue du Mont-Royal covers up to December 31, 2027, and support for the pedestrianization of avenue Lacombe up to December 31, 2028.

plan-urbanisme.description: The PUM and the concordance by-laws that each borough adopts to comply with it.

etapes.texte: Ahuntsic-Cartierville amends its urban planning by-law for the planting, maintenance, protection and felling of trees. Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie revises its urban planning, special projects and demolition by-laws, and Saint-Léonard does the same for its special projects and demolitions, after public consultations held on February 26 and February 11, 2026.

The borough lengthens its list of heritage buildings of interest, regulates housing and service establishments for people in residential instability, and amends its by-laws on demolition, special projects and site planning and architectural integration programs. A public assembly was held on March 18, 2026 and a written consultation from March 11 to 18, 2026.

The borough changes the heights, uses and building footprint ratio in the sector bounded by avenues Papineau, Émile-Journault and André-Grasset and rue Legendre Est. It also increases the permitted heights on sections of rue Lajeunesse, between boulevards Crémazie and Henri-Bourassa.

etapes.titre: Requests for extension to the ministry
etapes.texte: Ahuntsic-Cartierville requests twelve more months, until June 16, 2027, to adopt its concordance by-laws. L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève requests six more months, citing staff shortages, the complexity of its territory and the fall 2025 election.

Ville-Marie amends its urban planning by-law and its by-laws on special projects, demolition, authorization certificates and cadastral operations. Following the public consultation of March 25, 2026, the City revised the view corridor and height plans; the by-law allows a maximum height of 103 m on the block of the former terrasse Peel and requires approval for certain work within the declared heritage site of Mont-Royal.

Saint-Léonard acknowledges two correction minutes signed on March 19, 2026, which correct the name of a school and the identification of a building on boulevard Provencher. Ahuntsic-Cartierville then adopts its by-law on the demolition of buildings, after a public consultation assembly held on June 23, 2026.

aSurveiller.texte: L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève states it wants to present its project to elected officials starting mid-June 2026 and hold a public consultation in September or October 2026.

The Minister of Municipal Affairs has set June 16, 2027 as the deadline for Saint-Léonard to adopt all its concordance by-laws; other blocks are announced, including the replacement of the zoning by-law.
Ahuntsic-Cartierville requests an extension until June 16, 2027 to adopt its concordance by-laws.
Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension has until June 17, 2027 to update its by-laws; its zoning by-law must be replaced in 2027.

securite-publique.description: The City of Montréal's Service de police (police department): contracts, neighbourhood police stations, council motions.

etapes.titre: Loan for equipment and loan of a police officer
etapes.texte: The urban agglomeration council adopts a by-law authorizing a loan of $10,880,000 to buy and replace specialized SPVM equipment between 2026 and 2030. It also authorizes the loan of a detective sergeant to the RCMP team that enforces the Firearms Act, for three years starting January 7, 2026.

The City buys 11 patrol motorcycles, extends janitorial services at the headquarters by one year, and awards work to replace the oil heating system of the cavalry building at 1515 chemin Remembrance. It also awards a contract for meals for detained persons and extends maintenance of the call dispatch system software.

The City leases 50 parking spaces at 260 boulevard De Maisonneuve for headquarters vehicles. It renews the leases for the training centre in Anjou, neighbourhood police station 15 in Verdun, and neighbourhood police station 26 on avenue Mountain Sights.

The City enters into an agreement to supply 9 mm practice ammunition used for police firearms training, and extends the SPVM's mail pickup and delivery service by one year. It also retains suppliers for carpentry and painting services in the department's buildings.

aSurveiller.texte: "Fèves au lard" (beans) fundraising day at neighbourhood police station 46, on October 23, 2026; the borough of Anjou buys 62 tickets.
The port patrol boat and its trailer must be delivered no later than March 1, 2027.
The lease for the metro unit premises of neighbourhood police station 50, at 888 boulevard De Maisonneuve Est, starts on February 1, 2027.
The ACCES Tabac, Alcool, Cannabis and ACCEF committees are extended until March 31, 2027.
The work to replace the oil heating system of the cavalry building must be completed by September 30, 2027.

transport-collectif.description: What the City decides around the network: land sold to the STM, areas around stations, agreements.

velo.titre: Bikes: REV, bike paths and BIXI
velo.description: The Réseau express vélo, bike paths and bike lanes, and the BIXI bike-share system.
velo.enBref: This year, the City mainly bought equipment for the BIXI bike-share system, paid for work on existing bike lanes, and settled the occupation of Hydro-Québec land crossed by bike paths. Boroughs awarded maintenance and development contracts, and the City asked Québec for money for four new bike-related projects.

etapes.texte: Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie issued an ordinance that formalizes the bike lanes on avenue Christophe-Colomb between rues des Carrières and de Bellechasse and imposes mandatory manoeuvres on motorists up to Jean-Talon Est. Outremont authorized $100,000 for de-icing salt and abrasives to be spread, notably on its bike paths.

etapes.titre: Bike path repairs and sustainable mobility corridors
etapes.texte: City council added $3,400,000 to the contract with Bruneau Électrique inc. for sustainable mobility corridors in Ville-Marie and Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve, then approved Ville-Marie and Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension carrying out roadway and bike lane work, including repairs to the REV Lajeunesse between Jarry and Crémazie. Ahuntsic-Cartierville retained Déneigement et Excavation M. Gauthier inc. for spring cleaning of narrow bike paths.

City council awarded a sole-source contract worth $4,815,802.61 to PBSC Solutions Urbaines inc. for bikes, stations and docking points compatible with the BIXI system. The executive committee then retained Laser AMP, a division of ISE Métal inc., for $394,851.17, to supply the steel pavers used as a base for the stations.

Outremont tabled a draft by-law to convert the shared lane on avenue Lajoie, between Stuart and Outremont, into a one-way bike path. Le Plateau-Mont-Royal awarded Cojalac inc. work on rue Parthenais including a BIXI station, and the Sud-Ouest awarded Groupe Damex inc. the development of three green alleys and the electrical installation of a BIXI station.

etapes.titre: Requests for financial assistance from Québec
etapes.texte: City council authorized the filing of four requests for financial assistance to the ministère des Transports et de la Mobilité durable, for bike lanes and sidewalks on rues de Champlain, Saint-Jacques, Guy and Laurier. The City commits to paying at least half of the eligible expenses.

aSurveiller.texte: October 9, 2026: deadline to file complete financial assistance requests with the ministère des Transports et de la Mobilité durable.
The repair of the bike lane on rue De Louvain, between west of rue d'Iberville and boulevard Saint-Michel, is budgeted at $570,000 in 2027.
